The changed hunks are documentation only in docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new section (head lines 4816-4826) on GPT-OSS decode command buffers. The supplied units are unchanged surrounding text from head lines 1217-2025; they do not include the new section, whose patch excerpt is complete. The new text says GPT-OSS plain decode steps commit a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound, via GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers and CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding. It says results do not depend on the partitioning and that prefill keeps MLX defaults. This is a performance and scheduling tuning note.

No trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-storage behavior is changed by the supplied text. The surrounding material (prefix-cache, SSD stage, deadlines, MTP, calibration) is unchanged context. It does not alter T-041 (SSD prefix cache, SEC-035), and its descriptions are consistent with the threat model: media requests are excluded from prefix lookup, and the cache scope is not crossed.

Open integration question: the actual Swift implementation of the command-buffer limit is not supplied, so I cannot check its correctness. It is a hot-path change affecting only availability and performance (T-029/T-010-adjacent). The in-flight command-buffer limit of ten is mentioned only as motivation. I identified no concrete security regression from the documentation change.
